# `supersql` package reference

Import path `github.com/gosuda/supersql-alpha`.

## Package documentation

Package supersql is an embedded, single-process database that speaks a
conformant subset of PostgreSQL 18 SQL. A host opens a Catalog with Open (or
a database/sql Connector with OpenConnector, or a pgx/v5-compatible pool via
github.com/gosuda/supersql-alpha/pgx) and supplies a certified clock such as
github.com/gosuda/supersql-alpha/clock/local; there is no server, no network
listener, and no DSN.

OpenOptions.Clock is required and borrowed: the host owns the clock
provider's lifecycle and must close the database before closing it. Storage
layout, the SQL surface, and the conformance position are generated under
docs/reference by internal/tools/docgen.

### `func RestorePITR(ctx context.Context, baseBackupDir string, walArchiveDir string, targetTS clock.Instant, options PITRRestoreOptions) (*Catalog, PITRResult, error)`

RestorePITR restores baseBackupDir into options.Open.Directory, replays every
contiguous archived WAL segment from walArchiveDir with commitTS <= targetTS,
and opens the recovered database strictly at or before targetTS.

RestorePITRFromChain restores an incremental backup chain into
options.Open.Directory, replays contiguous archived WAL segments from
walArchiveDir with commitTS <= targetTS, and opens the recovered database.

SQLState returns the PostgreSQL SQLSTATE carried by an error produced by the

### `type Catalog`

Catalog is one opened native database. It owns the backend, workers,
transaction manager and session services, and borrows the host clock.



#### `func Open(ctx context.Context, options OpenOptions) (*Catalog, error)`

Open composes the native session stack over Directory and returns the owning
database: backend, transaction manager, control-plane stores and session
services. A fresh directory is bootstrapped in one atomic catalog statement; a
bootstrapped database is reopened from its durable manifest. The host-supplied
clock is borrowed, never replaced. Open never reads wall time, keeps no
package-level registry, and never constructs a clock of its own.


#### `func RestoreCheckpoint(ctx context.Context, backupDir string, options OpenOptions) (*Catalog, error)`

RestoreCheckpoint restores the backup at backupDir into options.Directory —
which must be missing or empty — verifies every manifest file and the
persisted certified fence, then opens the restored database under Open's
readiness rules: writable restoration certifies a fresh fence above the
restored frontier, while HistoricalReadOnly serves retained snapshots without
a synchronized clock.


#### `func RestoreEncryptedCheckpoint(ctx context.Context, backupDir string, encryptionKey []byte, options OpenOptions) (*Catalog, error)`

RestoreEncryptedCheckpoint restores an encrypted (or unencrypted) full
checkpoint backup from backupDir into options.Directory, verifies the
encryption key fingerprint, file checksums, and certified read fence, then
opens the restored database under Open's readiness rules.


#### `func RestoreIncremental(ctx context.Context, chainDirs []string, options IncrementalRestoreOptions) (*Catalog, error)`

RestoreIncremental validates a full-plus-incremental backup chain
[baseDir, inc1Dir, ...], verifies parent lineage, decryption keys, checksums,
and certified read fence, reconstructs the database at options.Open.Directory,
and opens it.


#### `func (database *Catalog) Close() error`

Close releases the session, allocator, transaction manager, backend and
workers. It is safe to call repeatedly and reports the first error while still
releasing every owned collaborator.


#### `func (database *Catalog) CopyFrom(ctx context.Context, statement string, source io.Reader, options CopyOptions) (CopyResult, error)`

CopyFrom executes one COPY ... FROM STDIN statement, reading records from
source until EOF. The caller keeps ownership of source; the engine never
closes it. Server-side COPY FROM 'file' and FROM PROGRAM are excluded
features and fail with SQLSTATE 0A000.


#### `func (database *Catalog) CopyTo(ctx context.Context, statement string, sink io.Writer, options CopyOptions) (CopyResult, error)`

CopyTo executes one COPY ... TO STDOUT statement, writing records to sink.
The caller keeps ownership of sink; the engine never closes it. Server-side
COPY TO 'file' and TO PROGRAM are excluded features and fail with SQLSTATE
0A000.


#### `func (database *Catalog) CreateHotBackup(ctx context.Context, targetDir string) error`

CreateHotBackup captures one certified closed snapshot — the backend file
set plus the fence secret — into targetDir, which must be missing or empty.
The backup is immutable and internally checksummed; RestoreCheckpoint opens
it at a destination. Historical-only databases re-publish their persisted
closed frontier.


#### `func (database *Catalog) CreateHotBackupWithOptions(ctx context.Context, targetDir string, options BackupOptions) error`

CreateHotBackupWithOptions captures one certified closed snapshot into
targetDir, optionally encrypting every backed-up file with AES-256-GCM when
options.EncryptionKey is provided.


#### `func (database *Catalog) CreateIncrementalBackup(ctx context.Context, baseBackupDir string, options IncrementalBackupOptions) (IncrementalBackupInfo, error)`

CreateIncrementalBackup captures one certified closed snapshot relative to
baseBackupDir (a full backup or an earlier incremental backup) into
options.Destination, copying only newly created or modified files and
recording unchanged files as inherited references.


#### `func (database *Catalog) Directory() string`

Directory reports the database directory this instance was opened on.


#### `func (database *Catalog) EnableWALArchive(ctx context.Context, archiveDir string, encryptionKey []byte) error`

EnableWALArchive enables atomic WAL segment archiving on an open database.
Every existing unretired WAL segment and every subsequent durable commit WAL
segment is atomically copied to archiveDir (encrypted with AES-256-GCM when
encryptionKey is non-empty) before WAL retirement can unlink it.


#### `func (database *Catalog) MaintenanceError() error`

MaintenanceError reports the most recent background maintenance failure, or
nil when every pass since Open succeeded. The loop exits on a fatal failure
and delivers it to Close; a long-running host observes the same error here
without closing the database.


#### `func (database *Catalog) Metrics(ctx context.Context) DatabaseMetrics`

Metrics returns a live snapshot of query, auto-ANALYZE, storage backlog, and
block-cache counters for the database.


#### `func (database *Catalog) Notify(channel, payload string) error`

Notify publishes a notification directly to all listeners on channel.
It validates PostgreSQL channel (<= 63 bytes, non-empty) and payload
(<= 8000 bytes) limits.


#### `func (database *Catalog) RunAutoAnalyze(ctx context.Context) (int, error)`

RunAutoAnalyze executes ANALYZE on every table whose accumulated mutations
have reached the configured auto-ANALYZE threshold, resetting each analyzed
table's pending mutation counter. It returns the number of tables analyzed.


#### `func (database *Catalog) Subscribe(channels ...string) *Subscription`

Subscribe registers an in-process Go listener on one or more PostgreSQL
LISTEN/NOTIFY channels. Channel names are normalized case-insensitively like
unquoted SQL identifiers.

### `type Connector`

Connector is a driver.Connector that owns one opened Catalog. Every Connect
creates a connection with its own session, so settings, prepared statements,
cursors, advisory locks, temporary relations and active transactions never
cross connections. The host owns close order: sql.DB first, then the
Connector, then the clock provider. Close releases the database, so no live
connection may outlive it.

##### Example: `OpenConnector`

ExampleOpenConnector runs the README quick start verbatim: OpenConnector uses
localclock.New(), sql.OpenDB adapts it, and the printed account proves the
committed rows read back.


```go
ctx := context.Background()
dir, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "supersql-example-*")
if err != nil {
	panic(err)
}
defer os.RemoveAll(dir)
if err := runReadme(ctx, dir, os.Stdout); err != nil {
	panic(err)
}
// Output:
Account: 1 | Alice | 50000
```

### `type Driver`

Driver cannot construct a connection by itself: a certified clock is not
expressible in a DSN, and no global provider lookup exists. Connections come
only from OpenConnector, which owns the clock's Catalog.

### `type OpenOptions`

OpenOptions configures Open. Clock is required and borrowed: the host owns
provider startup and shutdown and must close the database before closing the
provider, because a live database holds fences certified by that provider.


```go
// OpenOptions configures Open. Clock is required and borrowed: the host owns
// provider startup and shutdown and must close the database before closing the
// provider, because a live database holds fences certified by that provider.
type OpenOptions struct {
	// Directory is the database directory. Open creates it when absent.
	Directory	string
	// Compaction overrides individual storage backend resource limits when
	// nonzero; zero fields inherit DefaultCompactionConfig().
	Compaction	CompactionConfig
	// Clock is the certified time source borrowed by the database.
	Clock	clock.Clock
	// Maintenance bounds the background reclamation loop Open starts. The zero
	// value selects the defaults; Maintenance.Disabled stops the loop.
	Maintenance	MaintenanceConfig
	// HistoryRetention configures the durable MVCC history retention window.
	// Zero selects the default (24h); negative values are rejected by Open.
	HistoryRetention	time.Duration
	// HistoricalReadOnly opens the database without requiring fresh certified
	// readiness: no writes and no latest reads are accepted, only retained
	// historical snapshots are served. The clock may be unsynchronized.
	HistoricalReadOnly	bool
	// Parallelism sets the execution worker pool concurrency. Zero or negative
	// selects runtime.GOMAXPROCS(0).
	Parallelism	int
	// MemoryBudgetBytes overrides the shared query memory budget (default 256 MiB).
	MemoryBudgetBytes	uint64
	// TransactionMemoryBytes overrides the per-transaction in-memory staging limit (default 8 MiB).
	TransactionMemoryBytes	uint64
	// TransactionSpillBytes overrides the per-transaction spill limit (default 32 MiB).
	TransactionSpillBytes	uint64
	// MaxTransactions overrides the maximum concurrent active transactions (default 64).
	MaxTransactions	int
	// MaxOperations overrides the maximum concurrent snapshot/read operations (default 64).
	MaxOperations	int
	// Observer receives one QueryEvent after each completed SQL statement.
	// Nil disables per-query observer notifications.
	Observer	QueryObserver
	// SlowQueryThreshold marks statements whose duration meets or exceeds this
	// value as slow queries. Zero disables slow-query tracking; negative values
	// are rejected by Open.
	SlowQueryThreshold	time.Duration
	// OnSlowQuery is invoked when a statement's duration meets or exceeds
	// SlowQueryThreshold. Nil disables the callback while still incrementing
	// DatabaseMetrics.SlowQueriesTotal when SlowQueryThreshold > 0.
	OnSlowQuery	func(context.Context, QueryEvent)
	// EncryptionKey enables optional pure-Go AES-256-GCM at-rest encryption for
	// newly written SST runs, WAL files, and encrypted backups when set to a
	// 32-byte key. Nil disables at-rest encryption.
	EncryptionKey	[]byte
	// WALArchiveDir enables continuous WAL segment archiving into the given
	// directory for Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR). Empty disables WAL archiving.
	WALArchiveDir	string
	// WALArchiveKey optionally encrypts archived WAL segments with a 32-byte
	// AES-256-GCM key when WALArchiveDir is set.
	WALArchiveKey	[]byte
}
```
